scope: Others-only personal review queues, no review deadlines, automatic advance after a choice, static twelve-second ranking, smooth questions and staged Goodhart reveal without quotation marks.

checks: Time cannot advance an unanswered review card
Each of 21 authors sees exactly 20 other authors once
No next without a choice; choices remain immutable
Early finishers wait until everyone finishes
A non-author reviews every available reflection
Exact writing/ranking/question server deadlines and sleeping-client catch-up
Concurrent 21-person voting preserves exactly 420 votes and stable ties
The local host and three independent participant browsers join without accounts or names; the anonymous showcase and ranking are announced
The writing form has the agreed question without a helper line, accepts one reflection per person and starts the anonymous review automatically
Unanswered review remains in place beyond ten seconds, has no countdown/Next button, and faster voters wait
Each author sees exactly two other reflections, choices advance automatically, and the frozen ranking counts flowers only
Static ranking holds twelve seconds, questions cross-fade without background jumps, and Goodhart/quote reveal progressively without quotation marks
Host shutdown closes the classroom cleanly; state lives only in the running process
21 simultaneous independent browsers submit and complete 420 others-only card views / 420 votes in 38.8s, receiving the same exact tied ranking
No browser runtime errors or requests to external services
all.platform: Linux server binary and Chromium; Windows PE cross-build is validated separately

windowsBinaryChecks: All built web assets and illustration embedded byte-for-byte
CGO disabled; no Python/Node.js runtime or paid service required

limitations: Browser/service checks ran on Linux. Windows x64 PE and embedded assets were verified; native Windows execution was not tested.
Simulated independent browsers do not replace a classroom network test.
